ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Wilma Rudolph

code.originalText: End of six weeks of radiotherapy with daily temozolomide: blood counts, liver tests, Pneumocystis prophylaxis, fatigue, mood, tumor-treating fields and an early palliative care referral

text.paragraph: Review at the end of six weeks of radiotherapy with daily temozolomide. [S]

Ms. Rudolph returns on the first weekday after her last radiotherapy fraction. She completed all 30 fractions and took temozolomide every day without a break, the 42nd and last dose last night. Nausea was mild and controlled by ondansetron before each dose. She stopped dexamethasone a month ago and her fingerstick glucose readings came back below 120 mg/dL, so she stopped checking. She is more tired each week, sleeps after lunch and has worked only a few hours a day for the past two weeks. Her hair has fallen out over the treated area and the skin there is pink. She has had no headache, seizure, change in speech, weakness, fever, bruising, cough or fall. The weekly blood counts at the radiation clinic were normal in the first five weeks; the week 6 count was not drawn. She has read about tumor-treating fields and wants to talk about them. She has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-09-14; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Tired but well; weight 67.2 kg; blood pressure 118/74, pulse 80, temperature 36.8 °C
Alopecia over the left frontal field; grade 1 radiation dermatitis; incision healed
Speech fluent; strength full in all four limbs; finger tapping equal; gait steady
No leg swelling or calf tenderness

Three weeks of headaches on waking, with ten days of pauses in finding words and clumsiness of the right hand, in a previously well woman of 54: an intracranial lesion must be excluded. MRI of the brain with and without contrast booked for tomorrow morning, and neuro-oncology review booked
S — Synthetic presenting problem; no symptom of her real illness was made public. Superseded when the MRI showed a brain mass.

Left posterior frontal ring-enhancing mass, 3.8 cm, with central necrosis, surrounding edema and 5 mm midline shift, next to the language and motor areas; presumed high-grade glioma, with no primary cancer elsewhere on CT; tissue diagnosis pending
S — Synthetic imaging diagnosis before surgery; superseded by the pathology.

Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4, left posterior frontal lobe, MGMT promoter methylated, after gross total resection of the enhancing tumor; synthetic modern detail linked to her publicly reported brain cancer
S — Synthetic histology, molecular result and location; brain cancer is documented as the cause of her death (D), and nothing more about it was made public.

Late effects of childhood poliomyelitis: paralysis of the left leg in early childhood, treated with a metal brace, a special shoe, massage and heat, with full recovery of walking by about age 12 and a later career as an Olympic sprinter; no new weakness, fatigue or pain now to suggest post-polio syndrome
S — Documented childhood polio (D); the current absence of new symptoms is synthetic.
Vasogenic cerebral edema around the left frontal mass, with 5 mm midline shift, causing headache and contributing to the language and right-hand symptoms; treated with dexamethasone
S — Synthetic finding on the first MRI.
Steroid-induced hyperglycemia on dexamethasone: random glucose 168 mg/dL, with an A1c of 5.6% before steroids
S — Synthetic common effect of dexamethasone; resolved after the taper.
Lymphopenia from temozolomide, grade 2 (absolute lymphocytes 0.5 x 10^3/uL at the end of chemoradiation): Pneumocystis prophylaxis continues until recovery to grade 1 or better
S — Synthetic common effect of daily temozolomide with radiotherapy.

list.item:
Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, MGMT methylated, after chemoradiation (C71.1). Chemoradiation completed on schedule. Platelets 112 (grade 1) and white cells 3.6 with neutrophils 2.4 are expected at the end of daily temozolomide and will recover during the four-week break. ALT 48 and AST 39 U/L are a grade 1 rise, common with temozolomide; to be rechecked before adjuvant treatment. Fatigue at this point is mainly from radiotherapy and should ease over the coming weeks. We discussed tumor-treating fields: in the EF-14 trial, adding them to adjuvant temozolomide lengthened survival, at the cost of wearing scalp arrays at least 18 hours a day and possible skin irritation. She chose to start them with adjuvant temozolomide. [S]
Four-week break from temozolomide.
MRI of the brain with contrast in about three weeks.
Adjuvant temozolomide 150 mg/m2 on days 1 to 5, cycle 1 after the MRI, if neutrophils are at least 1.5 and platelets at least 100.
Tumor-treating fields device fitting arranged to start with cycle 1.
Palliative care referral now, alongside treatment.

Lymphopenia from temozolomide, grade 2 (D72.810). Absolute lymphocytes 0.5: the label calls for Pneumocystis prophylaxis to continue until lymphopenia recovers to grade 1 or better. [S]
Continue sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim three times a week.
Lymphocytes with each blood count.

Steroid-induced hyperglycemia (R73.9). Glucose 96 mg/dL a month after the last dexamethasone dose; resolved. [S]
Problem resolved; recheck glucose if steroids are needed again.

Late effects of childhood poliomyelitis (B91). No fall; legs strong; fatigue is explained by treatment rather than a new post-polio pattern, since there is no new weakness, muscle pain or intolerance of cold in the left leg. [S]
Continue home exercises at a gentler level; rest breaks.

tr.td: Blood count with neutrophils, lymphocytes and platelets
Hemoglobin 11.9 g/dL, white cells 3.6, neutrophils 2.4, lymphocytes 0.5, platelets 112: grade 1 thrombocytopenia and grade 2 lymphopenia
Blood count in week 6 of concurrent treatment

A deviation: not drawn in the last week of radiotherapy because the clinic's standing order was set for the Monday, a holiday that week, and was not moved. No harm resulted: today's count, a week later, shows platelets 112 and neutrophils 2.4, above the levels that would have stopped temozolomide, and she had no bleeding or fever. Corrective action: today's count; future standing orders are tied to treatment days, not a weekday

list.item: MRI of the brain within 24 hours and a neuro-oncology and neurosurgery plan within one week of presentation. Outcome by 2026-07-02: MRI the next morning; consultation three days after the first visit [S]

Maximal safe resection within two weeks of the MRI, preserving language and right-hand strength. Outcome by 2026-07-29: Gross total resection of the enhancing tumor nine days after the first visit; speech back to normal within days and right-hand strength nearly normal [S]

Radiotherapy with daily temozolomide started within six weeks of surgery and completed on schedule. Outcome by 2026-09-14: Started 26 days after surgery; 30 fractions and 42 days of temozolomide completed without a break [S]
Dexamethasone tapered off within five weeks of surgery, with glucose back to normal. Outcome by 2026-09-14: Off dexamethasone five weeks after surgery; glucose 96 mg/dL afterwards [S]
No falls, and walking independently, through treatment. In progress; target 2026-10-09 [S]

Follow-up: MRI in about three weeks; palliative care in two weeks. Review with the MRI result on the day adjuvant temozolomide starts. Call for fever, bruising, bleeding, a seizure, headache or new weakness. Next scheduled visit 2026-10-09: post-chemoradiation MRI result, day 1 of adjuvant temozolomide, the start of tumor-treating fields, and the palliative care plan. [S]
